topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by framing the learning goals and outlining how previously introduced concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Sensing infection and damage via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular criteria that allow the innate immune system to detect microbial presence and tissue damage while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and downstream signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular localization, receptor families, and intracellular signaling mechanisms that translate danger signals into inflammatory gene expression.

topics.label: Cellular recruitment and systemic inflammatory dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells coordinate the recruitment and migration of leukocytes into tissues and lymph nodes, alongside the pathological risks of excessive systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is terminated to permit tissue regeneration, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation and pathogen containment.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and introduces the topic of the following lecture.
